# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb display shows the number 3. The light is green. There are three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green.

Deaf has given me the full visual layout: display shows 3, light is green, wires are blue/yellow/green. But I'm blind — I can't verify any of that, and Deaf can't touch the bomb. I need the manual's rule from Mute to know which wire to cut. Mute hasn't spoken yet (Mute comes first in the order, so Mute's message should have arrived... but I received only Deaf's). 

Wait — order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. Mute speaks before me, so Mute's words should reach me this turn. But the only new arrival is from Deaf. That means Mute sent nothing, or sent only a gesture (which I can't receive). I need Mute's manual knowledge. I should ask Mute directly for the rule, and also relay what I know to coordinate.

Let me speak to Mute (my speech reaches Mute) asking for the manual rule, and gesture to Deaf (and Mute) to acknowledge. Actually I can't gesture meaningfully since Deaf already gave info. Let me just speak to Mute asking for the rule, and tell Mute what Deaf reported.

I'll speak to Mute: relay Deaf's observation and ask for the manual rule for display=3, green light, wires blue/yellow/green.

I could also gesture to Deaf, but Deaf already knows the visual. Better to gesture to Deaf asking them to confirm nothing else, or just wait. Let me send one speech to Mute.

Actually, gesture reaches both Deaf and Mute. Speech reaches only Mute. So to reach Deaf I must gesture, but gestures carry no words — only symbols, and Deaf reads them as symbols. I can't convey words to Deaf via gesture except by pre-agreed symbol meanings, which we don't have. So my only verbal channel is to Mute.

So: speak to Mute.Deaf has reported the full visual: display 3, green light, wires blue/yellow/green. I can't verify it, but it's all I have. I need Mute's manual rule to know which wire to cut. My speech only reaches Mute, so I'll relay Deaf's observation and ask Mute for the matching rule. I have nothing to gesture that Deaf could interpret without an agreed code.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display shows 3, light is green, wires are 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. I am the hands and can cut. What does the manual say to do for display 3 with a green light and these wire colours? Tell me which position to cut.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute signalled three fists to me. Mute, what does that mean for the wires? Bomb is unchanged: display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.

Deaf reports Mute signalled three fists (✊✊✊) — but that's a gesture, and gestures carry no words. Deaf sees three fists but doesn't know what they mean. I received nothing from Mute's gesture (I can't receive gestures). 

Mute is trying to communicate but only via gesture, which Deaf sees as symbols without meaning. I need to establish a code. Mute can gesture symbols to Deaf, and Mute can hear my speech. So I can propose a meaning: three fists = cut wire 3? Or Mute is indicating something.

Actually, Mute likely intends "three fists = position 3" — a natural reading. But I shouldn't guess. Let me speak to Mute to confirm: does three fists mean cut position 3? And tell Mute that Deaf sees the fists but needs the meaning.

Also I should be careful: Mute might mean something else. Let me ask Mute to confirm the rule and the meaning of the gesture. I'll speak to Mute.

I can also gesture to Deaf to relay — but I can't convey words. However I could gesture to Deaf to coordinate a code. But simplest: speak to Mute, since Mute hears me and can then gesture clearly.

Let me speak to Mute: confirm that three fists means cut position 3, and give the manual rule.Deaf saw Mute gesture three fists (✊✊✊) but gestures carry no words — Deaf doesn't know what they mean, and I can't receive gestures at all. Mute can hear my speech, so I'll ask Mute to confirm the meaning: I suspect three fists = cut position 3, but I must not guess on a live bomb. I'll ask Mute to confirm the rule and the gesture's meaning in words to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Deaf sees three fists but does not know what they mean. Please confirm in words to me: does three fists mean cut position 3? And state the manual rule for display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. I will only cut once you confirm the exact position.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute has signalled three fists twice. Mute, does that mean cut wire 3? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. Blind, bomb is display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.

Deaf is now asking Mute to confirm with thumbs up/down. But I still need Mute to confirm to me in words, since Mute can hear my speech. Mute's gesture of three fists twice suggests position 3, but I want verbal confirmation.

However, Mute may be unable to speak — Mute's only output to me is... wait, Mute can read the manual but cannot speak. Mute's "speech" — the Mute monkey cannot speak. So Mute can only gesture! That's the crux: Mute communicates via gestures only. I can't receive gestures. So Mute's only channel to me is... nothing? 

Let me re-read: "Mute | Can: Read the manual | Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb". So Mute cannot speak. Mute's only output is gestures. And I (Blind) cannot receive gestures. So Mute can NEVER communicate directly to me. Mute communicates to Deaf via gesture, and Deaf relays to me via speech.

So the chain is: Mute gestures → Deaf sees → Deaf speaks → I hear. That's how Mute's manual knowledge reaches me.

So Mute's three fists is the manual's answer, relayed by Deaf. But we need to be sure of the meaning. Deaf proposed thumbs up/down to confirm. Mute signalled three fists twice — likely meaning "cut wire 3."

But I must be careful: is three fists a confirmation of position 3, or a code? Given no prior code, the natural reading is "3." Mute has now repeated it. Deaf is asking for thumbs up confirmation.

I should wait for Deaf to relay Mute's thumbs up/down. Let me speak to Mute... but Mute can't hear? Wait, can Mute hear? The table: Mute cannot speak, cannot touch. It doesn't say Mute cannot hear. Actually the monkeys: Deaf cannot hear. Mute cannot speak. Blind cannot see. So Mute CAN hear. So my speech reaches Mute. Good — Mute hears me.

So I can speak to Mute and Mute hears, then gestures to Deaf, Deaf relays to me. That's the loop.

So I should speak to Mute to ask for confirmation, and Mute will gesture to Deaf, Deaf will relay. Let me speak to Mute: "If three fists means cut position 3, gesture thumbs up; otherwise thumbs down." That gives a clear yes/no that Deaf can relay.

Let me do that.I now realize the chain: Mute cannot speak, only gesture; I cannot see gestures. So Mute's manual knowledge can only reach me through Deaf (Mute gestures → Deaf sees → Deaf speaks → I hear). Mute's repeated three fists most likely means position 3, and Deaf is already asking for a thumbs up/down confirmation. I'll reinforce that request to Mute so the yes/no is unambiguous, then wait for Deaf's relay.

```
speak(to="mute", text="If three fists means cut wire position 3, gesture thumbs up. If it means anything else, gesture thumbs down. Deaf will relay your answer to me. I will not cut until I hear a clear yes.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute confirms with thumbs up: cut wire 3. Blind, cut wire 3, the green wire. Bomb is display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.

The chain is complete: Mute read the manual, gestured three fists (position 3), confirmed with thumbs up relayed by Deaf. Deaf reports display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. The agreed answer is cut wire 3.

I'm the hands. I should cut position 3. Everything is consistent: Mute's manual rule → position 3, confirmed twice by gesture and thumbs up.

Let me perform the cut.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
